fixed.problem: L3-github-1 (major): you closed #46 on GitHub and pressed Merge on its dependent #48 a second later. The app answered "Merging #48." and merged #46's closed work into main. Root cause: only the watcher's next poll checked what a dependent's branch held. ProjectPullRequests.merge built its order from the open list, so chainOf skipped the closed #46 as if it were merged, and handed the chain to the bare ReviewedPrMerge. The only R-lock guard there, rebuild_owed_for, was set by that poll. The session's merge got the check through DependentBranches.mergePort; the person's merge never did.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts "l3-merge, run L3" > "L3-github-1: A closed on GitHub, then Merge pressed on B before any poll ...", "... a merge the app makes by itself (Merge automatically after review) whose dependency was closed before the watcher read it ..." and "L3-github-1, sibling: A redone and cancelled after both were accepted ...". All three failed at 112227c: the press answered queued "Merging #2." and the retry merged B. apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts "l3-merge, run L3" > "L3-github-1, L3-github-2, L3-github-7: ..." also failed at the base sources. The control test (a poll between the close and the press) passed before and after.
fixed.how: ReviewedPrMerge.checkBranchesWith(check) and checkBranchNow(task) return a BranchVerdict {left, owed}. Compose wires them to DependentBranches.checkBeforeMerge, which runs PrTaskExecutor.rebuildTask with settleRecord as beforePush, the same check mergePort runs before a session's merge. run() calls it before the gate for every merge outside a session: the person's Merge, a card's Merge and the retry pass. If work went away, the review is void: the record is left to you with rebuiltWithoutSentence and one card, and nothing is merged. If the rebuild only dropped what main already has, the record moves to the rebuilt head and the merge goes on. If the check cannot run, the record is marked owed and nothing claims it (R-lock). At the press, ProjectPullRequests.merge runs this check before it answers when a chain task builds on a pull request that is no longer listed open and not merged on its record (buildsOnGone). If the record is left to you, the press is refused with the record's sentence. If the check is owed, the press is refused with notCheckedSentence, unless a folder wait applies (W15-05 path). I followed the verifier's sketch, but ran the check in the foreground at the press instead of marking owed and rebuilding in the background, so the answer reports what was actually found. ADR 0111 is amended (2026-11-15). The chainWorld and restarted() test wiring was updated to match compose.

fixed.how: ProjectPullRequests.read() keeps the open pull requests the view was read from (readView(project, listed)). For each chain record whose listed head differs from its reviewed commit, the press calls ReviewedPrMerge.headMovedNow(task, head). If keepsOwnChange shows the head still carries the reviewed change (for example after Update branch), it returns null and the merge goes on as before. Otherwise the record is settled the way the merge step settles a press whose head moved: settle(..., pressed=true) sets head_moved, writes the task reason and files one card, even when the record had been waiting for your click. The press is then refused with headMovedSentence and nothing in the chain is approved. Sibling: settle no longer files a second card beside a merge card the task already has open; that card takes the new words instead. This is the verifier's alternative (W15-05 pattern), not the bounded foreground merge. The fake daemon mirrors it with state.pullRequestPressFinds.

fixed.how: New quoted-title.ts balancedCut(text, max, cut, slack=15). It cuts with each screen's own cutter. If the kept part opens a quote it does not close, it keeps the whole title when that is at most `slack` characters over the limit, and otherwise cuts before the unclosed quote. request-words q() uses it. Siblings fixed with slack 0: the cancel line's stuck task title, event-lines' quoted titles (the session log, cut first and then its quotes made single) and the critic notification's title.

not_done.problem: L3-github-1 part 3: when B (still holding closed A) is merged on GitHub's website before any poll, A's record says only '#A was closed without merging.' No card says that A's change reached main through #B, and nothing offers Take this work out on A.

new_problems: The 'changed after the review' card (I merged it / Leave it open) and the rebuild cards stay open when their pull request is closed on GitHub without a merge. 'I merged it' is then wrong. Only a merge closes them now; this run decided only the merge case.

Siblings of L3-github-3 that still answer 'Merging #N.' first: a press on a PR whose check failed on GitHub after the last look, or that stopped merging cleanly before the next poll. The merge step finds out a few seconds later and the Overview then says '#N is not merged yet: the row below says why.'.

The press's 'could not check' path (the branch check finds the task folder busy or GitHub silent at the press) answers '#N is not merged yet: Forerunner first checks what it holds of the work it builds on. Press Merge again in a minute.'. That path has no boundary test yet; only the left-to-person and unchanged paths are tested.
